Verified CPython 3.12 symtable surface. Symbol has exactly 11 predicates (is_parameter,is_local,is_global,is_nonlocal,is_free,is_imported,is_assigned,is_referenced,is_declared_global,is_annotated,is_namespace); is_cell is NOT public. Naive name-based CHA gives 24.63 candidate callees per attribute call site (1.22M candidate edges / 49464 sites). 24.9% of sites have exactly one defining class (free precision); 24.0% have zero (module/stdlib path, must not be dropped); 50.7% of attribute calls have a bare-name receiver, making scope+binding resolution the highest-value reducer.

68.2% of parameters (30745/45092) carry NO type annotation. Declared-type receiver typing covers under a third of Python, so argument->parameter flow is the primary mechanism, not an optimization. Q4/Q8: relations renamed java_py_* -> py_*. One prefix per core language. lib_py_* is populated by the ENGINE from its external-identification pass, not by the parser. Parser emits only py_*; isExternal columns are parity slots always false.

Q3: Python 2 and 3 emit into the SAME py_* relations. No py2_* set, no skipped files; dialect is a column (py_module.pythonDialect). Because skipping is off the table, the tree-sitter grammar gap must be bridged: adopting the narrow intra-line rewriter with a py_source_bridge_edit audit row per edit (survives 3.13, keeps positions truthful) over lib2to3 whole-file reprint.

Q6: added py_type_inference relation (17 cols). Relation not columns because unions are 1:N (x=3; x='hi' is two rows; unionSize==1 is the monomorphic test). evidence ladder LITERAL/COLLECTION_LITERAL/CONSTRUCTOR_CALL/CAST/ISINSTANCE_GUARD/... with confidence CERTAIN|PROBABLE|POSSIBLE. Parser emits only CERTAIN+PROBABLE; POSSIBLE needs call resolution, is not oracle-checkable, and is the engine's to append. Resolves the OBJECT_CREATION tension: expression stays CALL, construction becomes an inference row.

Q10: IR exists to let Datalog compute a sound call graph then narrow it, by joins alone. Five layers; verifiability boundary between layer 3 (local resolution + certain inference, parser) and layer 4 (cross-module, MRO, flow, engine). Parser stops where CPython stops being able to answer. Build order follows measured data-flow path frequency, scope/binding spine first.

NOT OWNED BY A0-A5 - needs an owner outside this fleet. Written up in python-work/HANDOFF-parser-core-32k.md. Measured: tree-sitter Node binding parse(string) fails at exactly 32768 chars (2^15-1 ceiling), and the callback's RETURNED CHUNK has the same 32767 ceiling. It is a CHARACTER limit not bytes (29k chars of CJK = 62k bytes parses fine). java-parser.ts:43 already does the correct thing (streaming callback, 8KB chunks above 30000 chars) so Java is NOT broken today - 8% headroom. Residual concerns: chunk size itself capped at 32767; withRetry masks a deterministic failure with 3 retries and backoff; the constant is duplicated per language and belongs in one shared parser-core utility. Do NOT split source into separately-parsed pieces - that yields N rootless trees and does not reliably announce itself (a naive 2-way split of argparse.py produced identical class/method counts to the correct parse).

Deliverable #1 BUILT: src/test/python-oracle/. Pinned to CPython 3.10.4 by absolute path (never python3). emit_oracle.py emits ground truth from symtable (scopes, bindings, all 11 predicates) and ast (structure, spans, attribute writes). Harness asserts Appendix B invariants 1-11, computes precision/recall per entity kind, and CLASSIFIES every disagreement (MISSING/SPURIOUS/PREDICATE_MISMATCH/FIELD_MISMATCH/KEY_COLLISION/ORACLE_INTERNAL). Golden files record interpreter path + full sys.version and are REFUSED if the regime differs. Self-test: 81 assertions, mutation-based. symtable.SymbolTable.get_id() returns id() of the underlying object: stable WITHIN a process, different ACROSS processes. Emitting it verbatim would make every golden file differ run-to-run, violating Appendix B invariant #5. Caught by the harness self-test before any golden file existed. The oracle now emits a canonical pre-order ordinal instead, which fully serves the column's documented purpose (schema v6 section 2.2 c11: 'oracle cross-check handle only; never joined on'). NOTE FOR A3: py_scope c11 symtableId must be a deterministic surrogate, NOT the raw get_id().

IMPORTANT FOR A3. Scope-introducing nodes inside a function's defaults, decorators, parameter annotations, return annotation, or a class's bases/keywords are evaluated in the ENCLOSING scope, so symtable makes them SIBLINGS of the def/class, not children. Same for the OUTERMOST iterable of a comprehension. 'def f(x=lambda: 1)' -> the lambda is a child of f's parent. A walker that stops descending at a scope node loses them: found by sweeping the oracle over sqlalchemy, 34 of 563 files failed. Fixed in emit_oracle.py via _enclosing_evaluated_parts / _owned_scope_nodes; the parser must replicate this or its scope tree will be wrong on ~6% of real files.

THE BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS FALSE and I have implemented the corrected assertion. Asked to assert that 'symtable child order matches ast source order'. It does not: symtable orders children by symbol-table CONSTRUCTION order. For 'def outer(): @d(lambda:DEC) / def f(x=lambda:DEF, *, y: C[lambda:ANN]=2)' symtable yields [lambda@3, lambda@3, lambda@2, f@3] - not source order and not even line order. Asserting source order would fail on real code for the wrong reason. What actually protects py_scope.startColumn (whose PK depends on the ast<->symtable pairing) is: every symtable child pairs 1:1 with an ast scope-introducing node by identity (type,name,line), and the pairing is UNAMBIGUOUS BY COLUMN. Invariant 9a now asserts that, including the case that matters - two children indistinguishable to symtable AND sharing a column, which would be a PK collision.

COUNTER-INTUITIVE CPYTHON BEHAVIOUR, verified on 3.10.4, IMPORTANT FOR A3. A bare annotation with no value ('x: int') reports symtable is_assigned=True — the annotation reserves the local slot. is_referenced is False. My first version of the semantics test asserted is_assigned=False and FAILED; the oracle was right and I was wrong. Had this been hand-written into a golden file it would have shipped as a permanent wrong expectation. py_binding c10 (is_assigned) must be true for annotation-only declarations.

'from x import *' is ONLY legal at module level in Python 3; inside a function it is a SyntaxError ('import * only allowed at module level'). The oracle reports it as fatal SYNTAX_ERROR cleanly. Relevant to py_scope.usesWildcardImport: only a MODULE scope can ever have it set on a valid Py3 file.

VERIFIED ON 3.10.4, these gaps FORCED values into tier 1 that would otherwise be tier 2. (1) typing.get_overloads does NOT exist before 3.11, so @overload stubs are INVISIBLE at runtime - only the final implementation is in __dict__. OVERLOAD_STUB is therefore ast-only. (2) typing.final does NOT set __final__ before 3.11, so the FINAL modifier has no runtime witness and is ast-only. (3) inspect.getmembers_static does not exist on 3.10, so introspection must read cls.__dict__ directly - which is also safer, since attribute access invokes descriptors. (4) A class-body lambda is an ordinary function at runtime, indistinguishable from a def; only ast sees it.

MEASURED, not assumed: across 909 stdlib classes from 168 modules, category collisions occur in 8 cases (0.9%), all of one shape - PROTOCOL_TYPE + ABC_TYPE + GENERIC_TYPE (typing.Protocol, typing.SupportsAbs and siblings). Synthetic probing found one further real shape, DATACLASS_TYPE + EXCEPTION_CLASS_TYPE (@dataclass class E(Exception)). Modifier frequencies: ABSTRACT 55, SLOTS 53, HAS_GETATTR 25, HAS_CALL 23, HAS_SETATTR 4. So the tier-3 priority order governs under 1% of classes - worth specifying precisely, not worth agonising over.

My first tier-2 emitter excluded ABC_TYPE and GENERIC_TYPE when _is_protocol was set. That is a section 3.1 PRIORITY decision smuggled into the evidence tier, and it made the measured collision rate read as 0.0%. Removed: tier 2 now reports every predicate that holds and flags the collision, and the real rate is 0.9%. Recording because it is exactly the failure mode the tiering exists to prevent - a spec decision inheriting the authority of a CPython fact.

SCHEMA GAP, filed not fixed. 'from .rel import thing as aliased' is level>0 AND asname set. PythonImportKind has RELATIVE_MEMBER and FROM_MEMBER_ALIAS but no RELATIVE_MEMBER_ALIAS, so the shape is decidable from ast yet inexpressible. Spec decision (section 1.2): relativity wins, emit RELATIVE_MEMBER and populate aliasName c11 - nothing is lost because originalName/aliasName carry the alias, whereas choosing FROM_MEMBER_ALIAS would lose the level. The oracle emits residue='RELATIVE_MEMBER_ALIAS' on these rows so the count stays visible. If the count is material, adding the enum value is free (enum values are not the frozen contract).

SCHEMA DEFECT, filed not fixed and NOT papered over with an invented distinction. py_type.typeModifier lists both HAS_CALL and CALLABLE_INSTANCE, but a class defines __call__ IFF its instances are callable - the two are coextensive as written, so one value is dead. Options: (a) remove CALLABLE_INSTANCE (recommended, free since enum values are not the frozen contract); (b) redefine HAS_CALL as __call__ declared on this class vs CALLABLE_INSTANCE as callable INCLUDING inherited (both detectable: 'in cls.__dict__' vs hasattr). Until decided the oracle emits HAS_CALL only and never CALLABLE_INSTANCE, so a parser emitting it shows as a disagreement - the correct outcome for an undefined field.

For A3's decision table. '@abstractmethod' stacked OVER '@property' (property innermost) raises AttributeError at CLASS CREATION time: "attribute '__isabstractmethod__' of 'property' objects is not writable". It is not a SyntaxError, so ast parses it happily and the parser WILL see it, but tier 2 can never observe it because the module fails to import. Spec (section 2.2): classify per the normal property rule and note it; do not special-case broken code. The reverse order (@property outermost) is the correct idiom and yields a property with __isabstractmethod__=True.
